title: Investigate: the agent stopped starting jobs (2026-11-11, 22:29 CET)
note: The machine was on. The agent started its last job at 22:29:23 CET (while a 21-repository rollout begun at 22:28:30 was still running) and logged nothing more until the author rebooted at 23:14:31, although a job waited from 22:45. The author had unplugged the phone at 22:22 - a clue: some of the lab watches the phone. After the reboot (lingering on) the agent ran but picked up nothing new for about 20 minutes - most likely replaying old jobs, see replay-never. The journals of both boots are on the machine.

title: One shared way for a job to start, check and stop
note: A job prelude: fresh (a branch from GitHub's main, or stop), must (run, stop with a reason on failure), expect (demand a text in an output). Today a diverged clone made a chain stop at its pull while the script went on, writing onto main; land refused - but the job should have stopped first.

title: Jobs on the lab machine
note: Submit, wait, results, preemption - the agent's hands.

title: Jobs side by side, by the resources they hold
note: A job declares resources (phone:surya, repo:<path>, cpu-heavy); the runner starts any job whose resources are free; the board shows what runs together.

title: Never in the way
note: Updates switch over when idle; notifications only when something changed; waits show themselves.

title: A reconnect never replays finished jobs
note: 2026-11-11 23:34: after lab-agent connect (max jobs given as 50), the agent re-ran the session's old jobs - it could not see their results - fifty at a time, on the same repository clones; the author stopped it within minutes. Two replayed pin updates opened pull requests (both legitimate tad 0.4.0 bumps). 1002 jobs were moved to archive/2026-11-11 in the jobs repository and max_parallel set back to 1. A job must run once: the agent keeps its own record of jobs started, never runs a job older than itself unless asked, and connect never resets that.

title: The token is never in a URL
note: 2026-11-11: the process list showed the GitHub token inside git's remote URL (x-access-token in https://...), readable by any local process; it was also pasted into a conversation. Pass it through a credential helper instead, and rotate the token.

title: The voice must not depend on the hands
note: 2026-11-11: with the agent stuck, no alert could reach the author, and the author's messages could not reach the agent - both go through the agent. That night a GitHub issue mentioning the author served (grenudi/lab-machine#23). Better: the client sends urgent alerts straight to ntfy, and something outside the machine notices the agent's silence.

title: Every wait records itself
note: Recording is live: every submit --wait and wait appends to waits.jsonl beside the board (when, seconds, --on or unlabelled, the board's current project, the job, how it ended). Next: a gatherer bringing waits into the projects' data, and the observatory's view.
